MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 25, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:06 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good

consideration will be voted on separately.)

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN requested to remove item 5E from the Consent Calendar.

is made by the State Treasurer, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, TO
APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 25, 2020
 7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

NONE.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  CAL WATER PALOS VERDES WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT/CPUC UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Carmelo Sorce from Cal Water summarized the project cost timeline, factors that drove the
price increase to $96M and then $108M, steps the California Public Utilities Commission
(CPUC) took to validate the revised costs and the advice letter filed in July.

Angie Gilbride from Cal Water explained that the average rate increase for customers will be
$1 per day for the first year beginning in January 2021, which will then drop to $0.62 per day
the second year, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

Discussion ensued regarding the “additional costs” outlined in the staff report that could
potentially drive the cost up to $120M, and issues currently in dispute with contractors, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN inquired further regarding the disputes with contractors, and
if there have been any litigation costs associated with these disputes.

Greg Milleman from Cal Water explained that 7.84% is the allowable rate for return to
shareholders for capital improvements, and that there are approximately 24,000 customers
covered by this project, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR SCHMITZ inquired about the cost breakdown of a project, hoping to determine how
the percentages are split between cost of business, costs charged to rate payers, and amount
paid out to stakeholders. Greg Milleman explained that Cal Water invests in the cost to
construct the pipeline project, providing service to customers for the next 40-50 years (“Cost of
Service”). Cost of Service includes 7.84% payment to shareholders and bond holders for
investing funds in the company to provide the capital for the project.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked Carmelo, Angie and Greg for their work with the
City during this long project. He expressed concern regarding the project costs increasing from
an initial budget of $57M, rising to $96M and potentially ending up at $120M. He stated that
Cal Water selected the methodology, land and location for the project, and because of this he
is concerned about the fairness of how much of the $120M should be paid by Cal Water versus
just the rate payers. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN has contacted State representatives
and plans to discuss the system, because if it is happening to RHE, it is likely happening to
other cities as well. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN recommended that MAYOR SCHMITZ
pen a letter to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to preserve our right to object
to the $96M and additionally the potential $120M. He stated that he is ultimately seeking
fairness and equity within this system.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZUCKERMAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 25, 2020
   DIRECT STAFF TO DRAFT AND SEND A LETTER SIGNED BY THE MAYOR
  TO THE CALIFORNIA PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION REGARDING THE
  CONCERNS ABOUT THE INCREASE IN PROJECT COSTS BEING PLACED
  ONTO RESIDENTS OF THE CITY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN expressed concern with the fact that there is no pressure
for cost savings within this system, and that as costs go up within the project, shareholders
benefit. He also expressed concern about the close connections between utilities and
commissioners, and inquired about the 2% of dividends in contrast to the 7.84% given to
shareholders and bond holders. Greg Milleman replied that he would research this question
and provide a response to the Council at a later time.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

Further discussion ensued regarding the continued communication between Cal Water and
the City, the fairness of cost increases being placed strictly on the shoulders of rate payers
rather than shareholders, the lack of incentive for cost savings with the current structure, and
how statutory rates are determined.

B.  REQUEST TO APPROVE A TASK ORDER WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING FOR
  PROJECT SUPPORT SERVICES UNDER A MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT
  MULTI-YEAR SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA)

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council approve a Task Order with
  Willdan Engineering for project support services in the amount of $210,607.50.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Vanessa Munoz from Willdan commented on the reduction of Willdan’s estimate provided for
this Task Order, without a change or reduction in the scope of services. She also explained
that construction is planned to begin in approximately two years, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN confirmed that the scope of work did not change, and
thanked Willdan for reducing the estimate.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained the fee increase that took
place in 2019, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that this Task Order
proposal does not include construction oversight for this project, and that Willdan will return
with another Task Order for construction oversight estimated to be around $60,000, in
response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A TASK ORDER WITH WILLDAN ENGINEERING FOR PROJECT
  SUPPORT SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $210,607.50.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 25, 2020
   AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
reporting that Los Angeles County is seeing a steady decrease in the number of daily cases
and hospitalization rates. LA County case rates have dropped below 200 cases per 100,000
resident, allowing the County to begin to request waivers from the State to allow some K-6
schools to reopen for in-person classes.

Assistant City Manager Alexa provided the following updates regarding upcoming City Events:
  • Ice Cream Social Distance Event planned for September 4 from 4:00pm – 6:00pm at
  Ernie Howlett Park, providing drive-through pre-wrapped ice cream to participants.
  • Two additional Drive-In Movie Nights have been proposed for October 30 and
  December 19 featuring the movies “The Nightmare Before Christmas” and “Home
  Alone”.
  • The Hills Are Alive Race will be held in a virtual-only format from September 12 –
  October 12, and registration is now open.
  • The City Celebration has been re-envisioned to include a birthday video featuring video
  clips from residents and businesses, and a 2020 time capsule.
  • The Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament has been postponed to a date to be determined,
  possibly in January 2021.
  • The Mayor’s Breakfast Ride will also be re-envisioned. Early plans include highlighting
  various equestrian landmarks within the City, with residents doing self-paced individual
  rides, with videos of the Mayor accessible at each location on the map discussing
  specifics about each site and its amenities.
  • The Annual Parade in December cannot be held in its normal format, however the
  Parade Subcommittee is exploring ideas including neighborhood parades including
  Santa, carolers, Fire Department, and possibly a house decorating contest, allowing the
  community to celebrate and enjoy the season from their front yards.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained who makes up the various subcommittees for these
events, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked staff and the members of the subcommittees for their efforts to
create a sense of community without group gatherings.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) held a Special Board of Directors meeting on August 20, discussing policing
operations in the South Bay.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that there will be a Neighborhood Watch
Leadership Council meeting September 1 at 6:00pm, via Zoom.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported that a Regional Emergency Preparedness Committee meeting
was held last week discussing brush fires, including recent brush fires in Palos Verdes
Estates and Rancho Palos Verdes caused by illegal fireworks. The emergency evacuation
plan for PVPUSD was also discussed. COVID-19 responses by the Peninsula cities, and
recent peaceful demonstrations were also discussed. She also reported there will be an
Elected Officials Disaster Management training on August 26.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also reported a Regional Law Enforcement Committee meeting also took
place last week, where the ALPR systems on the Hill were discussed. The Lomita Sheriff
Station made a request to the Peninsula cities for funding of radar speed guns.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
AUGUST 25, 2020
 MAYOR SCHMITZ also provided a Waste Management update regarding the manure rate
increase that went into effect July 1, 2020. Waste Management will now be waiving the rate
increase until December 31, 2020, and credits will be provided to those who have already
paid the bills at the increased rate. She recommended reconvening the Waste Management
Subcommittee to review recent concerns of the equestrian community and continued
compliance with recent State legislation.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also reported that the City will submit an opposition letter to SB 1120 at
the request of California Contract Cities Association (CCCA).

MAYOR SCHMITZ also reported that through the monthly Mayor’s meetings, the Peninsula
Mayors met with leadership from Cox Communications to address widespread and ongoing
concerns across the Peninsula, especially with online-learning beginning this week as
schools begin.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2467 - EXPRESSING OPPOSITION TO PROPOSED STATE
  PLANNING AND ZONING LEGISLATION THAT USURPS LOCAL CONTROL AND
  IMPOSES UNFUNDED MANDATES, AND EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR ACTIONS
  TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN LOCAL LAND USE AUTHORITY AND LOCAL
  CONTROL

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council review and consider
  Resolution No. 2467, expressing opposition to proposed state planning and zoning
  legislation and expressing support for strengthening local land use authority and local
  control.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated she is pleased with the Resolution and expressed her
appreciation for the City of Torrance for spearheading this effort.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN echoed COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s sentiments.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated she is in general agreement with the Resolution in
protecting local authority in the area of land use, but felt the Resolution was too broad. She
stated that the City should continue to review pieces of legislation as they come out and register
objections to those that effect RHE negatively. She then stated that the legislature is reacting
to an immediate crisis of homelessness with bills that don’t correct the issues, and that some
of the legislation will have long term negative consequences.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested the option to list the bills in the Resolution as the City
of Torrance did, to make the Resolution more specific.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, emphasizing
the need to specifically object to incoming legislation that negatively effects the City. He
explained that much of the current housing legislation does not address affordable housing,
but focuses only on creating more housing.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN. He stated
that it is a structural issue, with a need for affordable housing not just more housing.

City Manager Grammer explained the challenges of listing bills within the Resolution, and
stated that staff will continue to track the different pieces of housing legislation in coordination
with the League of California Cities and California Contract Cities Association, and submit
position papers on individual pieces of legislation.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL objected to listing individual pieces of legislation in the
Resolution, and agrees that it will be beneficial to analyze individual pieces of legislation and
determine which ones will negatively impact the City.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
AUGUST 25, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2467, EXPRESSING OPPOSITION TO
  PROPOSED STATE PLANNING AND ZONING LEGISLATION AND
  EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR STRENGTHENING LOCAL LAND USE
  AUTHORITY AND LOCAL CONTROL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  GFOA's CERTIFICATE OF ACHIEVEMENT FOR EXCELLENCE IN FINANCIAL
  REPORTING

City Manager Grammer recognized the Administrative Services Department for led by
Administrative Services Director Whitehead for receiving the GFOA Certificate of Achievement
for Excellence in Financial Reporting.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 9:05 P.M. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting in memory of resident Shirley Jean
